LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.1: Whole Numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Whole Numbers, part of Numbers in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we write numbers in words and/or symbols? 2. Where do we write numbers in words or symbols?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of millions in real-life

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read and write numbers in symbols up to hundreds of millions in real-life situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. read and write numbers in words up to millions for fluency

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. round off numbers up to the nearest hundreds of millions in real-life situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. classify natural numbers as even, odd, and prime in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. apply operations of whole numbers in real-life

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Whole Numbers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of millions in real-life

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read and write numbers in symbols up to hundreds of millions in real-life situations

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. read and write numbers in words up to millions for fluency

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. round off numbers up to the nearest hundreds of millions in real-life situations

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. classify natural numbers as even, odd, and prime in different situations

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. apply operations of whole numbers in real-life

   Whole Numbers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify and write place value and total value of digits using place value apparatus

2. read and write numbers in symbols on number cards or charts

3. read and write numbers in words on number cards or charts and practise writing dummy cheques for different sums of money

4. work in teams to prepare and use place value charts to round off numbers

5. play a number game, make number cards, sort and classify numbers according to those that are even, odd, or prime

6. work out or perform 2, 3, or more combined operations in the correct order using digital 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify and write place value and total value of digits using place value apparatus
2. read and write numbers in symbols on number cards or charts
3. read and write numbers in words on number cards or charts and practise writing dummy cheques for different sums of money
4. work in teams to prepare and use place value charts to round off numbers
5. play a number game, make number cards, sort and classify numbers according to those that are even, odd, or prime
6. work out or perform 2, 3, or more combined operations in the correct order using digital 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Whole Numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: speaking, listening and team-work as the learner works together with others to prepare

and use place value charts to round off numbers.

● Critical thinking and Problem-solving: interpretation and inference as the learner works together with others to identify

number patterns.

● Creativity and Imagination: making observations as the learner plays games of creating number puzzles that involve number

sequences.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner works in teams and plays number games.

● Unity: as the learner works towards achieving set goals of making number puzzles.

● Peace: as the learner shares different roles in playing games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Financial Literacy: as the learner practices writing dummy cheques for different sums of money.

● Self-esteem: as the learner creates number puzzles that involve number sequences.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Languages: language skills are enhanced as the learner writes numbers in words.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of millions in real-life
2. read and write numbers in symbols up to hundreds of millions in real-life situations
3. read and write numbers in words up to millions for fluency
4. round off numbers up to the nearest hundreds of millions in real-life situations
5. classify natural numbers as even, odd, and prime in different situations
6. apply operations of whole numbers in real-life
